items.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999
items.q: I mean that’s like Phil Harris talking “Sixteen Tons.”

ctx.x: Well to their ears it’s music but it’s almost totally rhythmic and also even the way they make the records now, the rhythm is so much out there, farther than any melody that might even be there.

Well maybe I’m prejudiced, I can’t fathom listening to something when it doesn’t have melodic lines, they’re just talking it. I mean that’s like Phil Harris talking “Sixteen Tons.” Remember that song? “Sixteen Tons.” Or Rex Harrison doing “My Fair Lady.” I mean he did a great job, but he wasn’t singing a song. I want to hear — Bobby Darin, you know, who is my favorite singer.

A quick question about the union. It seemed like they had a fairly together system about, you just don’t walk out on a band, with the business of having to give two weeks. Let’s suppose you walked out on a band. What was the — what could happen to you?
